page: Microsoft Azure F32-16amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine from the Famdsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 3780 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression benchmarks all place in the top 10% of tested servers. Multi-threaded decompression is also strong, ranking in the top 25%. For machine learning tasks, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 425.32 tokens per second on small 135M parameter LLM models. However, multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations on Passmark and Redis fall into the average category.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F32-16amds_v7 offers a dense hardware profile, combining a high-frequency dedicated AMD EPYC CPU with substantial memory capacity and fast local NVMe storage. This resource density makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive applications, large-scale data decompression, and local database hosting where high-speed storage and large RAM buffers are required. It is also well-suited for single-threaded processing tasks and lightweight LLM inference workloads.
